cells.tense: You are choosing from clarity, and the choice is landing in the present.
cells.act: hold your shape under the weight
cells.ask: Name the commitment that is actually yours right now, and hold your shape under it — one clear no where a yes would blur it.
cells.core:
Something is arriving, and you can tell what it is. That's the thing worth trusting here — not the force of wanting it, but the plainness with which you can say this, not that. When the direction is chosen from that clarity, energy follows without a shove, and what enters your life arrives to meet someone who already knows where they stand.

Nothing about this needs to be loud. The question coming toward you can be answered without winning the argument around it. Name the commitment that's really yours and hold your shape under it — one clear no where a yes would blur it. That stillness costs something, and it's the price of choosing from clarity instead of compulsion.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's arriving, and you can say yes on purpose.
cells.verb: saying this and not that, and meaning it
cells.place: the door where what's new is showing up right now

cells.tense: Ahead of what is actually arriving, you brace and grip the outcome you have already decided should happen.
cells.act: look at the same thing longer, until it shows you more
cells.ask: When you notice yourself forcing a result, stop and look at that situation longer before acting — see what it shows you.
cells.core:
Something is arriving, and you've already decided what it has to be. The grip is tight and the timeline is yours, not its, and you can feel the strain of holding a door open that wants to open by itself. What's entering gets met as a thing to manage, so it arrives smaller than it is — and the effort of forcing it costs more than waiting ever would.

You don't have to force less. Look longer instead. When you catch yourself pushing an outcome, give the situation more time before you move — see what it shows you that the first look didn't. What you're inside has more to it than the version you're defending, and looking again is how that becomes available.

cells.tense: What is entering now finds you numb at a threshold that has already closed.
cells.act: do the thing in your own way, without proving it
cells.ask: Do a piece of the day in your own way, with nobody told and nothing proved.
cells.core:
There's a threshold near you and you're not crossing it. The direction that used to point somewhere has gone quiet, and what's arriving meets a shrug before it can show you what it is. It isn't that you stopped wanting. It's that wanting kept costing and you stopped paying — and now the present feels like something you've stopped answering.

Start smaller than the question. Do a piece of the day in your own way, with nobody told and nothing proved. That's not the old push returning. It's your own shape showing in one act, which is where direction comes back from.

cells.tense: Direction is running, and you would describe it as just how things have gone.
cells.act: put your own name on what is already yours
cells.ask: Take some move you make this week and set your name on it plainly, without calling it circumstance.
cells.core:
You're moving, and from the outside it looks chosen. From in here it looks like momentum — this is how things have gone, this is what you do. The steering happens; it's just not on the books as yours. The direction is real and the awareness of it is missing, which leaves you drifting inside a life you're actually driving.

You don't have to change the course. Claim the course. Take some move you make this week and set your name on it plainly, without calling it circumstance. Acting as the one who decided is already true. Saying it moves it onto the record where you can keep it.

attempts.check: The draft says what the person chooses and does — what is entering, how they meet it — but the record gives no history, no motive, no scene, so anything about why the direction lapsed or what they want next would be invention. A reader could say 'you don't know what I've been through,' and that's right; the cells stay on the mechanism and the act. The asks survive a wrong read because each one asks for doing, not for a feeling or a story. The sentence that serves me, not them: any line about arriving 'late' or 'at last' — it sounds like growth and says nothing they can hold; it stays out.
